extracted.intended_audience: scientists, engineers, and other practitioners considering or applying for DARPA program manager positions
extracted.subtask_short: applying to be DARPA program manager
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and informal selection criteria describing the role, expectations, and qualifications for DARPA program managers — who conceive, plan, and lead high‑risk R&D projects on short-term tours. Useful for prospective applicants and internal hiring stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceive, plan, and oversee high-risk R&D efforts
rubrics_metrics.description: Program managers conceive, plan, and oversee the high-risk R&D efforts for which DARPA is best known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They are expected to originate project ideas, set strategy and technical plans, and manage the execution of risky research efforts aimed at major breakthroughs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deep domain experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawing on deep industry, academic, defense, or government experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates should bring substantial background in relevant sectors (industry, academia, defense, or government) to inform judgment and program design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passion for pushing limits
rubrics_metrics.description: As well as a passion for pushing limits — program managers are expected to push the boundaries of what is possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A demonstrated drive to pursue audacious goals, tolerate uncertainty, and pursue disruptive approaches is valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define challenges and milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Program managers define the challenges and milestones that structure our R&D efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They must translate goals into concrete technical milestones and checkpoints that guide research progress and assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead all aspects and collaborate with performers/partners
rubrics_metrics.description: They lead all aspects of the work, collaborating closely with research performers and partners to refine approaches and zero in on the path to major breakthroughs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful PMs actively manage relationships with performers and partners, iterate on technical approaches, and align stakeholders toward breakthrough outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-term service with urgency
rubrics_metrics.description: Program managers typically serve less than five years, fueling a sense of urgency to deliver results quicker than virtually any other research setting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be prepared to accept a short tour and operate with accelerated timelines and high expectations for rapid progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active cross‑community communication
rubrics_metrics.description: They communicate actively with other leaders across the defense, scientific, and engineering communities to unearth potential solutions to new and future challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective PMs maintain broad networks, engage leaders across domains, and scout emerging ideas and collaborators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek outstanding individuals across basic and applied sciences
rubrics_metrics.description: We actively seek outstanding individuals across the basic and applied sciences with the skills to undertake the exciting challenge of being a DARPA program manager.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DARPA looks for top performers in both basic and applied fields who have the technical skills, judgment, and leadership capacity to run high‑impact programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probing for the next big thing / visionary curiosity
rubrics_metrics.description: Always pushing the boundaries of the possible, they constantly probe for the next big thing in their fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PMs should demonstrate intellectual curiosity, the ability to identify transformative opportunities, and a forward‑looking vision for technology impact.
